rows_withdrawn.draft_row: | S281 | sysexits(3), FreeBSD 15.1-RELEASE and Ports.quarterly manual page (legacy exit status codes for system programs) — https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=sysexits&sektion=3 | docs | A | FreeBSD's own statement of the pre-defined per-failure-class exit-code scheme and of that interface's current status | §DESCRIPTION deprecation sentence at snapshot byte 49849 and §BUGS at bytes 53809 and 53846; page dated May 9, 2024; snapshot .ufo/waves/round-55/w1/T55W1ScribeSources-receipts/sources/sysexits.html 59251 B sha256 1fc793a2, fetched 2026-10-28 | REJECTED: the page deprecates the pre-defined scheme and calls the choice of exit value often ambiguous, so it cannot ground one exit code per class; flip: an authoritative spec assigning an exit code per failure class without deprecating the practice | rejected | 2026-10-28 | 365d | — |
rows_withdrawn.reason: the document is already held as S090 (FreeBSD 15.1 sysexits(3), scope 'legacy and deprecated by its own text'), so a row would be a duplicate; the refusal corroborates the L1's. The deprecation evidence is offered for the lesson's Gate entry, not for a row.

corrections.defect: the teaches cell ends '...and the message text does not repeat the program's own verdict vocabulary'. §4.4 states no such rule: the word 'exit' never occurs in the page, and nothing in it mentions verdict vocabulary. The sentence the row quotes is followed by the casing rule (byte 6247) and the no-trailing-period rule (byte 6501), which the row does not state.
corrections.proposed_row: | S280 | Formatting Error Messages (GNU Coding Standards §4.4) — https://www.gnu.org/prep/standards/html_node/Errors.html | spec | A | the line shape of a noninteractive program's error message, its casing and final punctuation, and nothing about exit codes | §4.4 Formatting Error Messages @ fetched 2026-10-28 (page snapshot `.ufo/waves/round-55/w1/T55W1ScribeSources-receipts/sources/gnu-errors.html` 7147 B sha256 `54c55cd4`, sentence at byte 5020, forms at 5154 and 5415, casing rule at 6247, no-period rule at 6501; reader extraction `.ufo/evidence/round-55/assimilation/S280-gnu-errors.txt` sha256 `edcaf94b`) | "Error messages from other noninteractive programs should look like this: program:sourcefile:lineno: message ... or like this: program: message" — one program-prefixed line is the standard's shape; the message starts lower-case, ends without a period, and the section states no exit code | mined | 2026-10-28 | 730d | corpus/knowledge/scratch-root-contract.md, corpus/lessons/round-55.md |
corrections.scope: in place while the row is uncommitted; if it is already committed, the contract's correction form is a new row whose teaches opens 'supersedes S280 —' (as S047/S048, S160/S089, S268/S108 do for same-URL corrections)

S280.kind: appended as 'docs'; the round's own Gate calls it 'a normative standard (tier A)', so 'spec' is the consistent value (optional, included in the patch)
S280.anchor: correct as appended: the extraction file exists and its sha256 starts edcaf94b as stated; the page snapshot with byte offsets is offered as a tightening, not a fix
S280.why: §4.4 prescribes the line; the page never mentions an exit status (grep -c -i exit -> 0), and the GNU Coding Standards' node index has no exit-status node

S090.why_no_c2_row: its scope already reads 'legacy and deprecated by its own text' and its teaches anchors a usage exit of 64, not the lane's 2; a new row would be a duplicate URL
